findings.reason: the deliverable must tie the record's validity to the invalidation that dropped the cache (or have the project watch's reports update the record) and add a control that invalidates from the kernel watch, then reads, or it will regress the change-push freshness it is meant to preserve.
findings.text: §15 justifies trusting the detector's record with "This is sound because the detector stats every recorded directory on each pass and would have reported any other move", but the read that matters is served immediately after an invalidation whose source is not the detector: `reckon/serve.py:2805` calls `_invalidate_tree_views(docs_dir, changed_at)` and then `_served_index_rows(...)` on the change-stream thread, and the per-tree `_ProjectChangeWatch` (a kernel inotify watch, `reckon/change_streams.py:23`) invalidates at `reckon/change_streams.py:537` without stat-ing anything, while the fleet detector's fast pass that produces the record runs on its own short interval. A local write can therefore fire the kernel watch and reach the read before the detector's next pass, leaving the detector's record older than the change; a read that takes every other recorded directory's identity from it would treat the just-moved directory as unmoved, keep its persisted files, and hand `_index` rows that predate the change its own stream is pushing — the freshness bound §5 declares at 2 s — until the next fast pass. §15's three cases all run a detector pass before the read, so none covers the path the section's caller uses

findings.reason: the plan must either gate the first pass in §15 with the mechanism that would meet it (an arming pass that stats, and a read that waits for it) or record the first-pass failure as a new section, instead of narrowing §7's hard gate to the pass the repair happens to fix.
findings.text: §15's acceptance reads "After the merge, the coordinator repeats §7's live passes after the next restart and reports `/_index/reckon` on both passes, which must answer in under 1 s on the second pass", while §7's declared gate is "every `/_index` request answers 200 in under 1 s in both passes" and §15's own Why gives reckon's first read at 6.5 s, caught in the same `_reuse_covered` sweep this section removes. On a restart the detector's first pass only arms and returns (`reckon/change_streams.py:427-434` records no identities and stats nothing), so the first read after the restart has no record to take identities from and repeats the full sweep: the section does not repair §7's first-pass clause. §7's close comment names the second read as the failure and streams it to a new section, so with §15 landed the plan is complete with §7's gate still failing on its first-pass clause and no section owning it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module, symbol and section resolves at this revision: `reckon/metadata_index.py`, `reckon/change_streams.py`, `_fast_tree`, `_reuse_covered`, `covered_dir_identity`, `_dir_identity`, `_invalidate_tree_views`, `tests/test_a_read_trusts_the_detector_pass.py` (to be created, as §3–§14 cite their own new tests), and "§13's path".
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §15's acceptance gate is the second live pass only, while §7's hard gate is "every `/_index` request answers 200 in under 1 s in both passes", and §15's own Why attributes the first read's 6.5 s to the same `_reuse_covered` -> `covered_dir_identity` -> `_dir_identity` sweep the section removes.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §15 places every log under the run directory with a revision header and a closing `EXIT=` line, and puts suites on the fleet allocation, matching the path discipline §§10–14 use; no scratchpad or node-local path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the deliverable's names carry no plan label, stage name or ticket id: `tests/test_a_read_trusts_the_detector_pass.py` names the mechanism, and the prose describes what the read does rather than which section asked for it.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated soundness argument ("the detector stats every recorded directory on each pass and would have reported any other move") does not hold for the caller §15's own mechanism must serve: the served change read invalidates and reads in the same breath, and the invalidation that precedes it can come from the kernel project watch, which stats no directory.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §15 carries one deliverable (the covered-set read takes unmoved directories' identities from the detector's last pass and scans only the moved ones), one test file, and one acceptance.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §15 declares `plan-section-depends-on` `s15 -> #s14` and its prose names that edge ("This runs after §14, which shares `reckon/metadata_index.py`"); §14 chains to §13, which §15's deliverable reads ("by §13's path"), so no dependency it needs is missing.
